title: Branch-and-Bound Kernel Scheduler for Mixed-Precision Attention & SeqLen-Aware Selection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
We routinely need to pick the best kernel implementation for attention and matmul primitives across heterogeneous GPUs (A100, H100, T4) and for a wide range of sequence lengths (prefill and decode). Current heuristics are brittle: a few hand-crafted rules cover common cases but regress in tail scenarios (mixed-precision breakdowns, unusual seqlen spikes, or when KV-cache reuse creates different compute/memory profiles).

Goal:
Design and implement a branch-and-bound style kernel scheduler that combines fast microbenchmarks, an offline candidate pruning pass, and a lightweight online selector that is both architecture- and sequence-length-aware. The solution should: 
- Reduce p99 latency regressions caused by suboptimal kernel choices for uncommon seqlens.
- Automatically discover Pareto-optimal kernel variants (fp16/amp/q4/q8, fused attention vs unfused) for each model family and GPU class.
- Add a low-overhead runtime decision path usable for real-time requests (prefill + decode).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Offline profiling phase: run a compact search over kernel candidates using a branch-and-bound search that prunes dominated kernels early using a simple cost model (latency, memory footprint, and quantization error proxy). Build a candidate table keyed by (model-arch, gpu-class, seqlen-bucket, precision) with measured medians and variance.
2) Candidate compression: collapse similar kernels into a small set of Pareto representatives per bucket and compute conservative fallsafe choices.
3) Online lightweight selector: at request time, look up the nearest seqlen-bucket and GPU-class; consult a micro-cache of recent selections; if cache miss, use an amortized micro-probe (single batch of size 1 for decode/prefill sample) limited to 1ms extra tail to validate choice, otherwise fallback to conservative kernel.
4) Continuous autotune: schedule background experiments (low-ratio traffic or synthetic probes) to validate and update candidate weights, with rollbacks if quality or latencies regress.

Why branch-and-bound?
The kernel space is large (many precisions, fused/unfused, tilings). Exhaustive measurement is expensive. Branch-and-bound allows early pruning when a kernel is clearly dominated in latency and memory while still exploring diverse precision/memory tradeoffs relevant to quality.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: model-level quantization training, changes to user-facing API surface, and new hardware support beyond the three GPU classes listed above.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can automatically pick a kernel with <=5% higher median latency than the best-measured kernel for 95% of seqlen buckets across tested models (Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, Falcon-40B distilled).
p99 regressions relative to baseline heuristics reduced by at least 20% across our synthetic workload and customer traces (measured on dedicated bench infra).
Runtime selection overhead for decode requests is <=1.5ms p95 when probe path taken, and <=0.2ms p95 when using cached selection.
Candidate table generation pipeline produces a stable artifact and upload to S3 with metadata (gpu-class, model-family, seqlen-buckets, measured-stats).
Integration tests (unit + e2e microbench harness) covering fallback and rollback behavior are added and green in CI.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Micro-probing adds tail latency for cold paths. Mitigation: cap probe time, use conservative fallback and sample only <1% of production traffic initially.
Risk: Offline profiling may not generalize across model families. Mitigation: profile representative model families and add sentinel probes to detect model mismatches at runtime.
Risk: Quality regressions for quantized kernels. Mitigation: attach quantization-error proxies and require manual approval for any kernel that increases proxy above threshold.
Risk: State blowup for candidate tables. Mitigation: aggressive compression to Pareto set and TTLs for rarely used buckets.
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler (Dedicated) causing noisy performance. Mitigation: coordinate with Dedicated autoscaling team and run canaries on dedicated pools first.

Risk: Security/permissions for S3 artifacts. Mitigation: use tenant-segregated artifact prefixes and IAM policies; security review not required for algorithm changes but follow infra publish checklist.
metrics: Median token latency delta vs best-measured kernel per bucket
p99 latency across decode and prefill workloads
Probe frequency and probe-induced tail latency
Autotune convergence rate (#buckets stabilized per week)
implementation_notes: Prefer non-blocking reads of the candidate table and integrate with existing kernel-advisor cache layer.
Leverage existing microbench harness under infra/perf/bench to run offline probes on representative GPUs; avoid running large exhaustive sweeps on expensive instances.
Use a compact binary artifact (protobuf or flatbuffer) for candidate table with explicit versioning to allow rollbacks.
Make probe behavior configurable by runtime flags to quickly disable in emergencies.
Align seqlen-bucket boundaries with existing KV-cache fragmentation heuristics to avoid mismatches between prefill and decode paths.
test_plan: Unit tests for pruning logic and candidate canonicalization.
Microbench end-to-end test that validates selector picks expected kernel for synthetic trace of seqlens.
A/B canary on dedicated pool using 1% of traffic for 48 hours comparing new scheduler vs baseline heuristics.
Regression job in CI that fails if median latency increases >5% on smoke models.
Chaos test that simulates GPU class changes and verifies graceful fallback.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Offline profiling and candidate artifact generation; internal review of Pareto tables (week 1-2).
Stage 2: Deploy runtime selector behind feature flag to staging and run synthetic workload; monitor tail and probe overhead (week 2-3).
Stage 3: Canary 1% traffic on dedicated pools with telemetry dashboards; rollback if p99 diff > +10% (week 4).
Stage 4: Increase traffic share progressively (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with checks at each step; enable continuous autotune in background after 20% (week 5-7).
